title: Electrical networks: property, damage and interruptions

seo.title: Electrical network insurance assessment | ING Broker
seo.description: Identify electrical assets, ownership, breakdown evidence and external supply interruptions before assessing insurance and business continuity in Moldova.
seo.keywords: electrical network insurance, electrical damage, power interruption, company electrical installations, electrical inventory

content:
Assessing insurance for an electrical network starts with the applicant's property and the loss being considered. A line, transformer, company panel and a consumer's equipment are different assets. Supply can stop without damaging company property. Conversely, a local failure may affect one installation while other users remain supplied. Identify the actual situation before using a general description of an outage.

This article helps companies in the Republic of Moldova prepare a file; it is not an electrical-intervention manual. Competent specialists assess safety, works and technical cause. No offer for every network or operator compensation is confirmed here. The broker and insurer have different roles, and the terms must be checked in the actual documents for each request.

Define the property before calculating value

List installations and evidence of ownership or the interest being assessed. Separate operator assets, consumer property and rented or leased equipment. Explain any shared use through the relevant relationship. A transformer-station label alone does not identify all components or who bears each expense. A site's name should not replace the documented property and parties when choosing an amount for assessment.

Initially provide a descriptive inventory without sensitive security plans or details exposing vulnerabilities. If technical drawings are required, agree on recipient and channel. Confidentiality matters even for a publicly known installation serving ordinary business. An address being public does not justify publishing access arrangements. The initial commercial explanation should disclose what is necessary for its purpose, not every available operational record.

Prepare a useful installation inventory

Group equipment by category, site and function. Record available identifiers, installation year and significant changes. Attach relevant value and condition evidence. Mark decommissioned components rather than combining them with active property to inflate a total or reuse an old incomplete list. Similar names can describe different items, while different abbreviations may refer to the same component. Ask the responsible team where identification is unclear.

Separate purchase cost, installation, transport and other expenses relevant to reinstatement. Ask which valuation basis the proposal uses and check that everyone describes the same property. Accounting, historic and replacement values are not necessarily equal. Explain differences before selecting a sum or comparing premiums. An unexplained total does not establish that every component or associated expense has been accepted.

What does breakdown mean in the proposal?

Describe the observed defect without independently determining cause. Identify the affected component, observation time and available technical report. Insurer terms may have specific definitions; ask how they apply to the actual configuration. A defect, wear and scheduled replacement should not automatically be treated as one contractual category. The record needs facts, not a preferred label chosen before competent findings are available.

Retain inspection history and unresolved recommendations. Disclose problems known before the request. Do not delete a report or present planned work as a new incident. Accurate assessment needs chronology. Risk acceptance and examination of an event are distinct from holding an inventory or making a payment. A renewal should not be presented as a retrospective solution to already known circumstances.

A supply interruption alone does not prove material damage

Record whether supply stopped, was restricted or the issue affected only the company's installation. Use operator communications and competent findings where available. Moldelectrica publishes continuity and transmission-service quality indicators. They describe monitoring, not an individual incident's cause or a right to policy compensation. A general performance measure cannot replace the specific evidence required to understand a company's own situation.

Ask separately about property damage and the consequences of an external interruption. If proposed terms do not explain the distinction, request an answer for the business scenario. A general continuity statement must not become a promise that every stoppage will be paid. Connect the explanation to actual definitions, limits and conditions instead of filling the gap with another company's experience.

Which activity depends on the installation?

Describe processes that stop, such as production, refrigeration, pumping or communications. For each, identify what is needed to explain the economic effect. Similar transformers may support very different operations. Equipment power or purchase value alone does not calculate a loss. Explain the connection between the component and the activity served rather than assuming the asset amount describes every business consequence.

Use specialist information to plan diagnosis, access, procurement and return. Estimates are not guaranteed deadlines. Separate expenses that continue from those avoided during shutdown. Where interruption protection is being discussed, ask how the required event is established and relevant sums calculated. The planning timeline and the contractual assessment have different purposes, even where both concern the same period of inactivity.

Spare parts and compatibility

Identify reliance on a single supplier or special order. Similar dimensions do not establish a replacement's compatibility or safety. This article recommends no substitutions or modifications. Prepare questions for competent people and retain technical replies relevant to time and expense planning. An organizational checklist cannot replace their assessment or authorize a change merely because a component appears in a commercial catalogue.

Distinguish confirmed stock and delivery information from indications. An online listing does not prove immediate availability of the correct part. Update the description when model or service arrangements change. Do not carry an old estimate into renewal or expansion without checking. A supplier's dated confirmation and an internal assumption should remain separate so management can see the actual uncertainty in the recovery plan.

Describe works and operation in stages

New installation, tests and ordinary operation should not be merged into one unexplained period. Identify actual stage and handover records. Explain works inside a site that remains operational. The reviewer needs to distinguish planned operations from assets already used. This description does not require public switching instructions, operational access information or a new engineering plan created simply for the insurance enquiry.

Ask which documents apply to the relevant stage. Insurance for operating property does not automatically provide identical treatment for every installation or test. A contractor agreement does not replace the owner's assessment. Keep commercial responsibilities, technical documents and insurance replies separate. Confirmation within one process must not be used without justification as proof that another process or stage has already been accepted.

What to check before comparing cost

Compare inventory, sites, period and defined risks. The premium is the amount paid for insurance. The excess is the insured's share of a loss under the contract; exclusions identify situations outside protection. Read limits, sublimits, notification and the full contract documents, not only a first page or summary. Similar short descriptions do not establish equivalent conditions for the actual installation.

Ask separately about inspection, transport, fitting and other significant expenses. Listing them in a request does not include them in the policy. A comparison table can link each business requirement to the reply and supporting document. Resolve contradictions before choosing. A lower price does not compensate for an unexplained difference in the property, period or conditions considered by the proposals.

Document a stoppage without improvised intervention

Personal safety and specialist instructions come first. This article asks for no component access, measurements or manoeuvres to take photographs. Retain permitted information about timing, communications and relevant documents. Do not alter equipment or history to simplify the file. Competent people and procedures establish cause. Administrative evidence collection is not a reason to enter an unsafe installation or perform electrical work.

Check notification and request the necessary document list. Preserve initial findings and dated additions. Do not promise payments to colleagues or customers before insurer assessment. Accounting evidence alone does not establish contractual acceptance. Technical reports, invoices and policy conditions need consideration together. A report revised by a specialist should remain connected to its earlier version instead of silently replacing the factual history.

Example: a production line stops

Imagine a company observing a stopped line and requesting competent inspection. Administration retains supply communications and separates internal observations from information about the external network. This hypothetical illustration describes no actual customer. It establishes neither cause nor operator liability or insurance inclusion. It shows which questions should remain distinct before anyone announces a technical, legal or financial conclusion.

Finance records repair expense, additional spending and production effects separately without counting one amount twice without explanation. After findings, review relevant insurance documents and notification requirements. The company does not purchase retrospective protection or treat renewal as a remedy for a known problem. A complete-looking spreadsheet is less useful than an honest record identifying the facts and replies still outstanding.

What changes when a new consumer is connected?

A new production line or charging station may change the business's dependence on its electrical installation. Retain commissioning date, equipment documents and the updated inventory. Authorized specialists assess the technical requirements. This article sets no permitted power and recommends no protective-device or connection changes. An internal investment approval is not technical authorization or an automatic amendment of insurance terms.

For economic planning, identify which activities can continue if the new consumer stops and which equipment needs checking before return. Separate investment costs from existing expenditure. Insurance discussion should concern the current installation rather than its pre-expansion description. Keep changes dated and explain the new dependencies so an old asset list does not misleadingly describe today's operational circumstances or supported activity.

Frequently asked questions

Does company property insurance include every power outage?

Do not assume so. Property damage and supply interruption alone require separate questions. Availability and terms of possible protection must be checked in the actual documents.

Who can establish the cause of failure?

Competent technical specialists. The broker can explain documents and assessment steps, but replaces neither technical findings nor the insurer's decision on compensation.

What should I send initially?

A descriptive inventory, general location, installation stage and main questions. Sensitive diagrams, system access and confidential records should not be sent through public forms.

Can a public tariff be used as my network's price?

No. An individual proposal depends on assessed information and conditions. This article provides no confirmed tariff or promise of policy issuance.

Next step

Request a discussion with ING Broker about assessment and intermediation possibilities. The broker explains options and arranges insurance where possible; acceptance and claims belong to the insurer under the contract. This guide confirms neither product availability nor individual coverage.
